_comment: One checking policy per use case. The Round 2 brief notes that a single one-size-fits-all approach rarely works: a customer-facing chatbot has a tight latency budget and low risk tolerance, while a batch decision-support tool can afford deep checks. Same engine, different policy.

customer_chatbot.name: Customer support assistant
customer_chatbot.notes: Customer-facing and latency-sensitive. Tier 1 runs asynchronously; anything it would have caught inline is handled by holding the consequence, not the text.

internal_copilot.name: Internal knowledge copilot
internal_copilot.notes: Staff-facing with a human already in the loop, so a moderate latency budget buys inline escalation.

decision_support.name: Regulated decision-support tool
decision_support.notes: Batch and regulated. Latency is nearly free here, so every flagged item gets full escalation.
